sources.title: KC Border, The Second Welfare Theorem (January 2001; version 26 January 2016)
sources.scope: Full eight-page note: second-welfare valuation support statement, Scitovsky/resource sums, local-nonsatiation closure, relative continuity and alternative convexity definitions.
limits: The note invokes separation without proving the needed open/noncompact theorem. The chapter supplies that input independently.

Strict contours are relatively open in X; they need not be ambient-open for arbitrary convex X. The chapter separates their convex sum from the ambient interior of the free-disposal resource set instead.
The note calls the semistrict mixture condition convex and distinguishes weak convexity; the chapter explicitly uses convex weak upper contours and proves convexity of strict contours directly.
The chapter supplies the omitted cheaper-bundle upgrade, nonnegative-price/disposal proof and ownership-balanced transfers. No source example is copied.

sources.title: Daron Acemoglu, MIT 6.254 Guest Lecture: Social Choice and Voting Theory (6 May 2010)
sources.scope: Weak-order domain, Pareto, IIA, finite Arrow statement and decisive-coalition proof; Condorcet and single-peaked median definitions and proof.
limits: Arrow proof reconstructed independently with explicit almost-versus-strong decisiveness and every three-alternative propagation step. No fourth alternative is required.

Slide 18 names the reduced coalition decisive between p2 and p3 in the branch with social p3 strictly above p2; its winning orientation is p3 over p2. The chapter uses an explicitly oriented partition table.

Slide 29 states the supporting coalition with peaks strictly above the median; the median itself and coincident peaks must be included using peaks at least the median. The chapter handles these counts explicitly.
Social ties are allowed; the minimal-coalition proof retains the weak reverse branch. Dictatorship constrains strict dictator comparisons, not the treatment of that voter’s indifferences.
No Gibbard–Satterthwaite theorem, agenda equilibrium or strategy-proofness extension is used or claimed proved.

sources.title: Tilman Börgers, Econ 603 General Equilibrium Theory Lecture Notes (14 October 2021), Section 8(a)
sources.printed_mapping: Physical and printed page numbers coincide; relevant Section 8(a) is pages 35–38.
sources.scope: Actual web-extracted income-aggregation definitions, positive-versus-normative representative-consumer distinction and common-affine-Engel statements.
limits: Direct PDF retrieval returned HTTP 403; no retained PDF bytes, local text artifact or viewed page-image claim. No retry or access workaround.
The source explicitly omits both aggregation proofs. The chapter proves its own differentiable product-open-income-domain equivalence instead of attributing an inspected proof to these notes.
Common slopes in the chapter may have negative components on bounded income intervals; nonnegative demand there does not impose global income monotonicity.
The original notes are not distributed. Later law-of-demand/uniqueness/existence sections and the cited MWG book are not relied on as inspected proofs.

proof_resolution: New finite open/noncompact separation argument; explicit downward-resource-set interior avoids topology slippage. All Arrow directions/tie cases and the product-income converse are independently derived, not imported from terse source steps.
